When I was younger, I would always resent having to put away my Legos -- the saga of the beard man and the alien had not yet concluded to my satisfaction. Yet my mother forced me to clean up.

It was a chore, normally, but I figured out that by cleaning only certain parts of the mess I could more or less create maps. So from that day forth I would always go through sagas of empires and radiation removal efforts in the last stages of my Lego time as a sort of cooldown for that day's creative venturing.

How have you guys learned to turn boring activities into fun ones?
I learned how to make dull things interesting...
I accepted that not everything I will have to do in life will be interesting.

I'd like to say so, but most of the time it just doesn't work for me. However, one thing does help reduce the mental strain, even if it won't make boring things fun.

That is, dividing large tasks into small sections (digestible for your brain, so to say). Say you've gotta vacuum your flat, or mow that lawn. Whether you simply divide your work into smaller squares, or abide some logical rules or algorithms, it's much easier to finish something if you know in advance you don't have to swallow it all at once, but have smaller pieces to chew on.
